tier_reason: The README Performance section has a head-to-head table against RabbitMQ 4.3: 64,532 vs 108,000 msg/s (1.67x), 25,381 vs 113,667 (4.48x), 24,232 vs 106,906 (4.41x), and 21,157 vs 23,217 at 64 KB (1.10x). The benchmark client is public (src/amqp-go/cmd/perftest/main.go) with reproduce commands, but the hardware is given only as 'Apple Silicon, 16 cores' with no chip model, and no Go toolchain version is stated, so this is first-party evidence with partial methodology: tier C.

corrections.workload: Durable queues with persistent messages and publisher confirms (up to 1000 unconfirmed publishes in flight per producer, the perftest default), fsync enabled on both brokers, 1 KB bodies (plus one 64 KB run), 1/10/30 producers with the same number of consumers, 20-second runs, consumer prefetch 100, manual acks. Figures are steady-state medians of the per-second consumed rate. Both brokers were driven by the same amqp091-go-based perftest client, and the queue was declared with no x-arguments, so RabbitMQ used its default classic queue type.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark on one Apple Silicon Mac; no chip model or Go version is stated. There is an environment asymmetry: RabbitMQ 4.3 ran in an OrbStack ARM64 Linux container with in-container storage, while StrangeQ ran host-native on macOS. The disk and fsync paths therefore differ, which could favour StrangeQ. The comparison is single-node against a default-configured RabbitMQ classic queue; StrangeQ has no clustering or HA. Numbers were measured 2026-07-14. The 'I used AI to build StrangeQ' wording comes from the author's Show HN title (2025-10-31), not the README: the author says an LLM wrote the code. Adoption is very low (5 stars).

notes: The claimed_speedup numbers match the README exactly, and license (MIT), stars (5), last commit (2026-08-29), non-fork and non-archived status all check out. The only real correction is where the AI-built quote comes from: it is the HN Show HN title (item 45767055), not the README. Otherwise the record is accurate.
